content.text: ▪︎HTN associated w/ MI, HF, stroke, & CKD
: sympathetic/RAAS overactivation, defect in natriuresis, variations in cardiovascular/renal development, ⇡ intracellular Na/Ca levels
: pheochromocytoma, Cushing’s syndrome, coarctation of the aorta, hyperparathyroidism, drugs (OCPs, NSAIDs, cocaine, stimulants, venlafaxine)
▪︎fundoscopic exam: +/- hemorrhage, papilledema, cotton wool spots, arteriolar
» when to suspect ⇢ severe or resistant HTN, onset <30yo, diastolic HTN onset >65yo
: ⇡ SCr ≥50% after starting ACEI/ARB, unilateral small kidney,
: hypokalemia w/ urinary K wasting, adrenal mass
: paroxysmal ⇡ BP; triad of HA, palpitations, & sweating
: UE SBP > LE SBP, ⇣/delayed femoral pulses
fasting glucose, lipid profile, TSH, UA, EKG
: weight loss, DASH diet, smoking cessation, salt restriction ≤1500mg/d, potassium intake 3.5-5g/d, aerobic exercise 90-150min/wk, ≤2drink/d for ♂︎, ≤1drink/d for ♀︎
Threshhold for initiation of pharmacological TX:
: combination therapy w/ fixed-dose single pill preferred for
▪︎⇡ dose at 1mo intervals or add additional agent if BP remains elevated
▪︎gout: avoid thiazide diuretics		▪︎post-MI: beta blockers, ACEI/ARB
